_note: Vendor figures transcribed 2026-09-18 from the NVIDIA architecture whitepapers themselves, not product pages or secondary sources, with table and page cited per card. All peak_tflops_dense values are dense, not sparse, and for the tensor rows they are the FP32 accumulate variant, because torch.matmul and torch._scaled_mm accumulate in FP32. Both whitepapers print each tensor row as dense/sparse, with the sparse figure carrying footnote 2, 'Effective TOPS / TFLOPS using the new Sparsity Feature'. Using a sparse or an FP16 accumulate number as the denominator would halve or quarter the reported efficiency, and is the easiest way to get Part B wrong.
_accumulate_note: NVIDIA lists FP16 tensor throughput twice, with FP16 accumulate and with FP32 accumulate, the former exactly twice the latter. cuBLAS runs torch.matmul on half inputs with CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, meaning FP32 accumulate, so the FP32 accumulate row is the honest denominator. The FP16 accumulate figure is kept below as peak_tflops_dense_fp16_accumulate for reference and must not be used unless you deliberately enabled reduced precision reduction and say so.

derivation.bandwidth_gb_s: 384 bit bus by 21 Gbps over 8 bits per byte is 1008 GB/s. The whitepaper prints 1008 GB/sec directly.
derivation.fp32: 16384 CUDA cores by 2 FLOP per clock by 2.52 GHz is 82.6 TFLOPS. Whitepaper row 'Peak FP32 TFLOPS (non-Tensor)' is 82.6.
derivation.tf32: Whitepaper row 'Peak TF32 Tensor TFLOPS' is 82.6/165.2. 82.6 is dense, 165.2 is sparse.
derivation.fp16_bf16: Whitepaper rows 'Peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' and 'Peak BF16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' are both 165.2/330.4, so 165.2 dense. The FP16 with FP16 accumulate row is 330.3/660.6 and must not be used for torch.matmul.
derivation.fp8: Whitepaper row 'Peak FP8 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' is 330.3/660.6, so 330.3 dense. The FP16 accumulate row is 660.6/1321.2. Note whitepaper footnote 4: this FP32 accumulate figure was corrected in v2.02, so an older copy of the PDF gives a different number.

derivation.bandwidth_gb_s: 512 bit bus by 28 Gbps over 8 bits per byte is 1792 GB/s. The whitepaper prints 1792 GB/sec directly.
derivation.fp32: 21760 CUDA cores by 2 FLOP per clock by 2.407 GHz is 104.8 TFLOPS. Whitepaper row 'Peak FP32 TFLOPS (non-Tensor)' is 104.8.
derivation.tf32: Whitepaper row 'Peak TF32 Tensor TFLOPS' is 104.8/209.5, so 104.8 dense.
derivation.fp16_bf16: Whitepaper rows 'Peak FP16/BF16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' are both 209.5/419, so 209.5 dense. The FP16 accumulate row is 419/838.
derivation.fp8: Whitepaper row 'Peak FP8 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' is 419/838, so 419 dense.
derivation.fp4: Whitepaper row 'Peak FP4 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate (FP4 AI TOPS)' is 1676/3352. 1676 is dense and 3352 is sparse. The product page headline of 3352 AI TOPS is therefore FP4 with sparsity, exactly twice the dense rate, not four times, and never a valid denominator for a dense measurement.
